newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO troops seize forbidden arms in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO troops seize forbidden arms in Bosnia.

text.p: International peacekeeping troops in Bosnia have seized unauthorised weapons, including mortars and an anti-tank missile launcher, from Serb and Croat forces, a NATO spokesman said on Wednesday.

Major Simon Haselock, spokesman for the NATO-led peace force, said a Czech peacekeeping patrol near the village of Pucari in Bosnian Serb territory had stopped a truck and found it carrying two mortars, a missile and an 82mm recoilless gun. These arms were confiscated, he said.

The Czechs then went back to the truck's base and found an SA7 missile, a rifle, 200 rounds of small arms ammunition, two grenades and an anti-tank missile launcher. This "unauthorised" equipment was also confiscated.
"We have sought, as you can imagine, an explanation from the 1st Krajina Corps as to what was going on," Haselock told a news conference.

At Kobiljaca, near Sarajevo, an inspection of an HVO Bosnian Croat militia barracks turned up two unauthorised armoured anti-aircraft vehicles. These had no weapons in them, but were also confiscated, Haselock said.
The December 1995 Dayton peace accord for Bosnia laid down strict controls on the storage and movement of weapons held by the former warring factions.

Weapons confiscated by peacekeeping troops are generally destroyed, often by crushing them with a tank. All three combatant factions have been found guilty of arms violations, with the Serbs being the most persistent offenders.
